children: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright warned oil traders not to expect Iran’s latest diplomatic push to produce a rapid breakthrough in the Strait of Hormuz, Bloomberg News reported Sunday.

Iran is preparing to discuss a temporary shipping arrangement with Gulf nations in Oman. However, reports indicate that Monday’s meeting is unlikely to produce a signed agreement. Wright said alternative transit routes are moving an estimated 10 million barrels a day of crude oil and refined products, keeping supplies flowing even as the market remains tight.

Continued uncertainty around Hormuz could keep a geopolitical premium embedded in crude prices, benefiting some oil producers while raising fuel, transportation and manufacturing costs. Tanker operators and insurers also face elevated risks. A credible shipping agreement could reverse part of that premium, although fresh attacks in the region suggest volatility may persist.

Wright also used his visit to Vienna for the International Atomic Energy Agency’s annual conference to increase pressure on Tehran over its nuclear program. He said the United States prefers negotiations but remains determined to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

International inspectors have been unable to verify Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium since U.S. and Israeli attacks on its nuclear facilities in June 2025. The IAEA also has reported signs of activity around Pickaxe Mountain, a fortified location suspected of supporting nuclear work, although the agency has not confirmed what is happening there.
Washington is demanding that Iran stop enriching uranium and dismantle its centrifuge program. Wright said nuclear fuel could instead be supplied from outside the country.

Separately, Wright said the Energy Department is nearing long-term agreements intended to strengthen domestic uranium production. The United States remains dependent on imported nuclear fuel, making expansion of the domestic supply chain strategically important for utilities and advanced-reactor developers. The department has committed billions of dollars to expanding U.S. enrichment capacity and reducing reliance on foreign suppliers.

title: Energy Secretary warns oil traders against betting on quick Hormuz deal
